text:
Dear Dr. Morrison,

Thank you for agreeing to consult on this 22-year-old gentleman who has experienced frequent pulmonary infections dating back to infancy, around four months of age. He recently required hospitalization for an episode of pulmonary Pneumocystis jirovecii infection. In addition, over the past year, he has exhibited a rather peculiar and stubborn fungal onychodystrophy across several fingernails.

Initial laboratory evaluation revealed pan-hypogammaglobulinemia, with profoundly diminished total serum IgG, alongside markedly low circulating IgA and depleted IgM levels. Extended immunophenotyping demonstrated that his switched memory B-cell fraction is markedly diminished. In contrast, his overall CD4+ T-cell percentage is strictly within reference range, showing neither elevation nor depletion.

Regarding his pulmonary status, high-resolution imaging demonstrated clear lung parenchyma without bronchiectatic remodeling, and there was no evidence of atypical bronchiolar inflammation. He has never developed ventilatory failure, and he has not displayed reactive airway constriction during these episodes. Multiple respiratory cultures have ruled out atypical mycobacterial pulmonary disease. 

Review of systems is otherwise benign. He has no history of repeated sinus disease, denies longstanding watery stools, and shows no indications of colonic inflammation. On physical examination, he appears well. His vitals are normal, and chest auscultation is clear. Abdominal exam shows a soft, non-tender abdomen with no hepatic enlargement or splenic enlargement, and there is no palpable adenopathy. He works in accounting, does not smoke, and his family history is non-contributory.

I would be grateful for your comprehensive clinical assessment and any recommendations regarding further immunological investigations or therapeutic steps.

Sincerely,

Dr. Evelyn Reed, MD
